hook.text: A buyer and seller each know their own valuation but not the other's. Can any mechanism guarantee efficient trade?

buildup.text: Efficient trade means: if the buyer values the item more than the seller, a deal always happens. Seems simple.

discovery.text: Myerson and Satterthwaite proved it: no mechanism achieves efficiency, honesty, and voluntary participation together.

twist.text: This explains why negotiations fail even when deals should happen. Private information destroys guaranteed efficiency.

climax.text: Middlemen, brokers, and platforms exist to overcome this impossibility—adding value by reducing information gaps.

punchline.text: Some deals that should happen can't—by math.

quiz.question: What does the Myerson-Satterthwaite theorem prove?
options: No mechanism guarantees efficient trade with private information
